admission: Operator-directed: the aarch64 VMware build worker is entirely the project's to reconfigure. Native builds on that worker only; no other host, no publication, no signing.
scope: First native aarch64 kernel, world, poudriere jail and port build at the selected source and ports revisions. It confirms that x11-wm/hyprland builds natively on aarch64 with the ports#28 workaround. No package feed, image, VM or laptop result exists. Nothing here admits the worker to the release graph or qualifies aarch64.

runs.reason: PACKAGE_FETCH_URL was written unescaped, so ${ABI} expanded empty and no package could be fetched. Stopped and corrected.
Stopped deliberately: without ALLOW_MAKE_JOBS each builder compiled llvm19 and rust single-threaded, which would not finish inside the bound. The built packages were kept.
Out of memory: llvm19 and rust's bundled LLVM, both at 8 jobs together, had llvm-tblgen processes killed by the kernel ('failed to reclaim memory') on 16 GiB with 2 GiB swap. Not a compile error.

runs.summary: Queued 16, built 16, failed 0, skipped 0, then testport of x11-wm/hyprland passed.

dependency_build_times.devel/cargo-c: 00:43:54 (mostly crate fetch stalls before the IPv4 preference was set)

hyprland_build.package_note: testport does not keep the target package in the repository; dependencies built here (rust, llvm19, mesa and others) are in /usr/local/poudriere/data/packages/16aarch64-daemonarchy. No feed or package identity is claimed.

hyprland_testport.conclusion: ports#28 is confirmed natively: hyprland 0.56.2_2 builds, stages, passes stage-qa and check-plist, and installs and deinstalls cleanly on aarch64 with devel/llvm19 once precompiled headers are disabled. This confirms a build, not a runtime: under VMware the guest cannot start Hyprland (gap 2).

admission.native_inspect_worker_allocation: Not applicable. native/inspect-worker-allocation.py relays to the inspection socket of a native/qemu-worker.py-supervised QEMU guest. This worker is a VMware guest with no such supervisor or socket, so nothing was run and no allocation record exists.
admission.release_graph: Not admitted. The release graph's capacity and identity admission for the aarch64 worker is still to be defined and recorded.
capacity_notes: 16 GiB with 2 GiB swap cannot build llvm19 and rust concurrently at 8 jobs each. Use one builder for LLVM-class ports, or add memory.
The 200G disk is below docs/aarch64.md's 400 GiB sizing.
